items.title: 3 Consumer Stocks That Fall Short
items.summary: Most consumer discretionary businesses succeed or fail based on the broader economy. Over the past six months, it seems like demand trends may be working against them as the industry’s returns were flat while the S&P 500 was up 11.8%.

items.title: 1 Value Stock with Competitive Advantages and 2 Facing Challenges
items.summary: Value investing has produced some of the world’s most famous investing billionaires, including Warren Buffett, David Einhorn, and Seth Klarman, who built their fortunes by purchasing wonderful businesses at reasonable prices. But these hidden gems are few and far between - many stocks that appear cheap often stay that way because they face structural issues.

items.title: Airbnb Just Rallied 21% in a Month: Take Profits, or Buy More?
items.summary: Airbnb just posted its best single-session surge in years and climbed past every analyst target on the board, which puts shareholders in an uncomfortable spot where both trimming and buying carry real consequences.

items.title: 1 Growth Stock with Explosive Upside and 2 We Question
items.summary: Growth is oxygen. But when it evaporates, the consequences can be severe - ask anyone who bought Cisco in the Dot-Com Bubble or newer investors who lived through the 2020 to 2022 COVID cycle.

items.title: 3 Large-Cap Stocks with Questionable Fundamentals
items.summary: Large-cap stocks are known for their staying power and ability to weather market storms better than smaller competitors. However, their sheer size makes it more challenging to maintain high growth rates as they’ve already captured significant portions of their markets.

items.title: Could Expedia (EXPE) Stock Keep Rising as B2B Growth Fuels its Next Phase?
items.summary: Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) raised its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $16.05B–$16.22B (representing 9%–10% growth), topping the Wall Street consensus estimate of $16.01B. The company also lifted its full-year gross bookings outlook to $129.5B–$130.8B. items.title: Expedia Executive Sells 3,133 Shares for $1 Million
items.summary: An Expedia insider disposed of more than 3,000 shares after a strong 12-month run for the stock price.

items.title: Executive Sells $1.4 Million Worth of Travel Stock, Following 54% Rally
items.summary: Dzielak retains 105,335 directly held shares valued at $33.55 million, plus 15,525 derivative securities, signaling continued confidence in the travel platform.
